text:
The Activity:

Spend six minutes planning and presenting a quick talk to tell each other all about yourselves. Both people should prepare a presentation and listen to each other’s at the end!

Follow the steps below to see how to use your six minutes!

One-minute first ideas:

  • Think about the type of presentation you want to do – are you going to do “A History of Me” from when you were born to now, or are you going to do something about how you are now?
  • Think about the important things to include – some of it might be facts, like your age or what foods you like, and some of it might be trickier to explain, like your feelings about particular things or what your personality is like. You can decide what you want to share, and what you think is important.


Two-minute planning:

  • Make notes of what you are going to say. Don’t write every single word, because presentations sound better when you speak rather than read out your notes.


Two-minute practising:

  • Practise saying your words a few times. This will help you check if it feels about the right length, and also make sure your notes help you remember everything you want to say.


One-minute presentation:

  • Decide who is going to go first. The other person will get to speak afterwards!
  • Make sure you speak clearly so your audience can hear what you are saying.
  • Use your notes to help you remember what to say!
  • When you’ve finished, spend a minute listening to the other person’s presentation.
